use_case_summary: Large-scale RAG for legal research: 30M+ documents (court opinions, briefs). Primary flow: user query -> approximate retrieval (FAISS/OpenSearch hybrid) -> dense-embedding top-K -> cross-encoder rerank -> final answer generation. Goals: reduce end-to-end cost per query while preserving or improving legal precedent recall and ranking quality. Strong need for A/B/canary rollouts and evals-driven migrations to avoid regressions.
notes:
Company background: Archimedes builds a legal research assistant used by law firms and in-house counsel. Heavy on long documents (opinions, dockets). Index size ~30M docs, nightly incremental ingestion. Currently using a mix of self-hosted FAISS + on-prem metadata store. Reranker is a licensed cross-encoder (expensive) used on top 200 candidates; embedding model is an older mpnet variant.

Sales / Prod notes (shorthand):
- 2026-02-18 kickoff call (ff_20260218_ArchQF_kickoff) — AE + SE + Head of Search present.
- POC ask: demonstrate migration from licensed cross-encoder -> Redwood-optimized smaller reranker + updated embedding family with A/B eval.
- Primary KPIs: nDCG@10, MRR, worst-case precision on precedent retrieval. Target: no >2% drop in nDCG vs current baseline.
- Infra requirements: ability to index 30M vectors, nightly delta ingest < 3 hours, query QPS burst ~200, sustained 60 QPS.
- Latency targets: reranker p95 < 220ms (end-to-end < 350ms), cold-start tail especially important.
- Cost target: reduce per-query compute by ~40% vs today; target cost per query <$0.008. Very cost-sensitive across large law-firm deployments.
- Security: must run in customer VPC or on-prem; DPA and SOC2 evidence required. Data residency in US-only for some customers.
- Evals: Archimedes has assembled an eval set (1,200 canonical queries + human judgments). Want Redwood Optimize integration to run automatic regressions and produce human-reviewable diffs.
- Quote from Head of Search: "If we lose recall on precedents it's a showstopper — we need measurable eval parity before rollouts."

Technical constraints / notes:
- Current reranker is expensive at scale (per-query GPU time high). Looking to move to a two-stage approach: light-weight re-ranker at retrieval time + optional heavy cross-encoder for critical queries. Wants automatic fallback routing by policy.
- Concern: embedding migration changes nearest-neighbor neighborhoods; needs revalidation across 30M index, sample + full-run eval plan discussed.

Timeline & activities:
- 2025-12-02: SE did infra sizing estimate (RI-TICKET-9842).
- 2026-01-14: shared eval set and scoring script (drive:/evals/arch_qf/eval_set_v1.csv).

- 2026-03-02: internal eval review call (ff_20260302_eval-review) — initial embedding candidates show slight nDCG uplift but reranker replacement has mixed results.

Open items / blockers:
- Need reproducible eval runs on full sample (not just 1k queries) to quantify regression risk.
- Legal wants explicit data residency language before any Private deployment.
- Cost model: Archimedes requests per-route cost simulation for their 3 weighted query classes.

Next steps (short):
- SE to deliver canary plan (10% traffic split) + rollback triggers (nDCG delta threshold + human-alert).
- Send formal pricing + dedicated capacity sizing by 2026-03-17.
- SOC2 / DPA exceptions review with security team (drive:/security/arch_qf/security_faq_responses.docx).
